mcp_server_schema_PUBLIC_in_expert_conte.discrepancy_with_agent_create_MCP_schema: A1B-AE.1 §4.1 captured a DIFFERENT MCP schema from /agentic/agents/create-agent with fields {name, url, description, authorizationScope, redirectUrl, token}. The two schemas likely correspond to different lifecycle phases: create-agent accepts OAuth2-style config (authorizationScope + redirectUrl + token), while Expert-config accepts transport-level config (transportType + authorizationType + url). iCoDer A1B-AE.3+ must support BOTH shapes depending on context.

multi_agent_composition_status_PUBLIC: COMING_SOON (not yet shipped). Listed capabilities: (1) direct agent-to-agent communication using A2A; (2) composition of complex workflows across multiple agents; (3) fine-grained control over agent interactions and data flow.
direct_expert_calls_status_PUBLIC: COMING_SOON (not yet shipped). Listed capabilities: (1) direct API access to individual experts; (2) integration of experts into custom workflows; (3) more flexible composition patterns beyond agent-based orchestration.
implications_for_icoder_a1b_ae_3: Expert model MUST include: id (canonical snake_case), name, description, system_prompt, mcp_servers[] (non-empty after A1B-AE.7).
Expert model SHOULD include: transport_type, authorization_type per MCP server.
Expert model MUST distinguish: client-provided 'id' vs server-generated 'id' (Corti uses client-provided for Experts, server-generated for Agents — A1B-AE.1 §2.1).
iCoDer A1B-AE.3 may ship Experts without mcp_servers[] populated (deferred to A1B-AE.7); but the model field MUST exist.
